programme.title: NHK Newsline
programme.desc: The world of politics, current affairs, business and finance as they unfold and affect Japan, Asia and the world globally. Insightful analysis and news coverage of the stories of most relevance to Japan and the surrounding region reported from a Japanese perspective and relevance. Archive materials and live reporting provide a full picture of Japan and its place and significance in the world.

programme.title: The Factory Wonders
programme.desc: Comedians Reiji and Tsuyoshi of the duo Nakagawake and Suchiko explore the many wonders of Japanese manufacturing. They learn about the latest technology and even try their hand at expert skills.

programme.title: Time-lapse Japan
programme.desc: Cinematic visual journey across the bustling streets of Tokyo Japan, one of the most vibrant and unique cities ever. Japan's busy capital, Tokyo, mixes the ultramodern and the traditional, from neon-lit skyscrapers to historic temples.

programme.title: Newsline Asia 24
programme.desc: Asian economies are recovering despite global uncertainty. Japan's exports are rising, while China and South Korea see improved manufacturing. Southeast Asia is boosting infrastructure and green energy. Experts point to regional cooperation as a key driver.

programme.title: Magical Japanese
programme.desc: Discover the rich and magical world of the Japanese language, which reflects nature, history and culture. Each episode is dedicated to a specific subject, introducing unique and wonderful words and expressions that are related to it.

programme.title: Easy Japanese
programme.desc: Learn Japanese easy and fast in a fun way. These language lessons will teach you both basic expressions and grammar, and they also feature useful travel and culture tips.

programme.title: Culture Crossroads
programme.desc: Programme that answers questions about Japan from foreign viewers, looks at international exchange programs, and helps viewers be prepared for various natural disasters.

programme.title: Hello! NHK World Japan
programme.desc: We intorduce the contents and activities of NHK WORLD-JAPAN to make the station and programs known to more people all over the world. This is the window of the station to the world.

programme.title: Newsline Asia 24
programme.desc: Asian economies are recovering despite global uncertainty. Japan's exports are rising, while China and South Korea see improved manufacturing. Southeast Asia is boosting infrastructure and green energy. Experts point to regional cooperation as a key driver.

programme.title: Seasoning the Seasons
programme.desc: Documentary programme that allows viewers to discover more about the stunning Japan, through its incredible and long history, ancient traditions, local festivals, amazing and beloved food and daily life. Find out more about Japan's favorite citrus fruit, Ishigaki Island, "nabe" or hot pot, local train lines, Shinbashi, one of Tokyo's leading business districts, ''soba'' or Japan's beloved noodle, and much more.

programme.title: A Culture Built With Wood
programme.desc: Japan is home to diverse forests that make 70 percent of its land area. The wood from these forests has been an important part of Japanese culture for centuries in various ways, from woodwork to charcoal and lumber production. We explore different regions all over Japan, including Hida, Kishu and Kiso, to find out more about their connections with these beautiful forests that are shaping the lives of the locals in many ways and are an integral part of the country's rich cultural heritage.

programme.title: Ramen Japan
programme.desc: Ramen is a savory combination of umami-packed broth and perfectly cooked noodles. This program offers an encyclopedic view of this delectable dish, taking you on a journey across Japan to discover ever-evolving local variations. Join us as we explore a tapestry of local customs and food culture through the lens of ramen.

programme.title: Ukiyoe Edo-life
programme.desc: The traditional, everyday life of the inhabitants of Edo (Old Tokyo) lives on in the time-honoured woodblock prints called Ukiyo-e which were extremely popular during this period of Japanese history. Each episode of this show focuses on the story of an individual Ukiyo-e print and also reveals the way of life in Old Tokyo at this time as well as revealing the stories behind the images and the artists.

programme.title: Bosai: An Educational Journey - Season 1
programme.desc: This program explores the Japanese culture of Bosai. Since natural disasters are happening often, the country developed a culture of prevention from these catastrophes based on past experiences with disasters like tsunamis, floods, fires, earthquakes and nuclear damages. The program offers advice on how to deal with such terrible events.

programme.title: IMPACTS: Climates Change the World
programme.desc: Explores how climate change is transforming ecosystems, communities and economies across the globe. Through scientific research, real-life stories and expert insights, the program reveals the challenges and solutions shaping our planet's future in a rapidly changing environment.

programme.desc: Cinematic visual journey across the bustling streets of Tokyo Japan, one of the most vibrant and unique cities ever. Japan's busy capital, Tokyo, mixes the ultramodern and the traditional, from neon-lit skyscrapers to historic temples.

programme.title: A Culture Built With Wood
programme.desc: Japan is home to diverse forests that make 70 percent of its land area. The wood from these forests has been an important part of Japanese culture for centuries in various ways, from woodwork to charcoal and lumber production. We explore different regions all over Japan, including Hida, Kishu and Kiso, to find out more about their connections with these beautiful forests that are shaping the lives of the locals in many ways and are an integral part of the country's rich cultural heritage.

programme.title: Ramen Japan
programme.desc: Ramen is a savory combination of umami-packed broth and perfectly cooked noodles. This program offers an encyclopedic view of this delectable dish, taking you on a journey across Japan to discover ever-evolving local variations. Join us as we explore a tapestry of local customs and food culture through the lens of ramen.

programme.title: Ukiyoe Edo-life
programme.desc: The traditional, everyday life of the inhabitants of Edo (Old Tokyo) lives on in the time-honoured woodblock prints called Ukiyo-e which were extremely popular during this period of Japanese history. Each episode of this show focuses on the story of an individual Ukiyo-e print and also reveals the way of life in Old Tokyo at this time as well as revealing the stories behind the images and the artists.

programme.title: Trails to Oishii Tokyo
programme.desc: Amazing show that introduces Japanese food that can be obtained at Tokyo's famous food markets. programme.title: A Culture Built With Wood
programme.desc: Japan is home to diverse forests that make 70 percent of its land area. The wood from these forests has been an important part of Japanese culture for centuries in various ways, from woodwork to charcoal and lumber production. We explore different regions all over Japan, including Hida, Kishu and Kiso, to find out more about their connections with these beautiful forests that are shaping the lives of the locals in many ways and are an integral part of the country's rich cultural heritage.

programme.title: Ramen Japan
programme.desc: Ramen is a savory combination of umami-packed broth and perfectly cooked noodles. This program offers an encyclopedic view of this delectable dish, taking you on a journey across Japan to discover ever-evolving local variations. Join us as we explore a tapestry of local customs and food culture through the lens of ramen.

programme.title: Ukiyoe Edo-life
programme.desc: The traditional, everyday life of the inhabitants of Edo (Old Tokyo) lives on in the time-honoured woodblock prints called Ukiyo-e which were extremely popular during this period of Japanese history. programme.desc: Along with the strengthened manufacturing capabilities of various countries all around the world, "Smart Factory" has garnered a lot of attention in the global market. programme.title: Exploring Korean Literature
programme.desc: 2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They’ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel "One Left", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film "Parasite," and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel "Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel "Diary of a Murderer" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, "Hysteria," as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, "The Disaster Tourist", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->

programme.title: Exploring Korean Literature
programme.desc: 2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They’ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel "One Left", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film "Parasite," and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel "Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel "Diary of a Murderer" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, "Hysteria," as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, "The Disaster Tourist", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->

programme.title: Exploring Korean Literature
programme.desc: 2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They’ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel "One Left", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film "Parasite," and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel "Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel "Diary of a Murderer" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, "Hysteria," as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, "The Disaster Tourist", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->

programme.title: SHOW K-POP
programme.desc: Music has crossed borders, but the charts are still bound within them. A stage in Seoul and lightsticks in Brazil, early-morning streaming in Manila and fan accounts in Paris. What moves K-POP today are the people around the world listening to the same song at the very same moment. “SHOW K-POP” is the one and only global chart show for everyone. And it all begins on October 19, 2026. Three Promises OF THE FANSThe main characters of the chart are the fans. Through TikTok and Mubeat, viewers step right into the broadcast. Every vote you cast and every comment you leave will help shape this music chart show. We’ll build this together with the fans, and complete it together with the fans.BY THE FANSStars are made by the fans. Every episode features at least one rookie group, giving you the chance to get to know the names the world has yet to know. We’ll create the moments when an artist you’ve just discovered becomes your ultimate bias. FOR THE FANLowering language barriers and raising the excitement. This is a show that’s conducted entirely in English from start to finish. There’s no need to wait for subtitles or rely on translations. We’ll bring the stories fans are most curious about in a way that resonates with fans around the world. The one and only global standard chart show, made together with K-POP fans worldwide. Premieres October 19, 2026 | LIVE every Monday at 6 PM (KST)https://www.showkpop.comPlease catch the reruns!Broadcast Schedule (KST)- Monday: 6:00 PM (Live Broadcast / Premiere)  - Friday: 12:50 PM, 6:00 PM- Saturday: 6:00 AM- Sunday: 10:50 AM, 8:50 PM- Monday: 2:00 AMThere is no on-demand replay available. And the government has unveiled and promoted a roadmap "Manufacturing Innovation 3.0," as part of an effort to enhance the competitiveness of the domestic manufacturing sector. Moreover, a domestic major company Samsung Electronics has provided a smart factory solution in order to boost mutual growth with small and medium-sized businesses. SmartBiz Accelerators introduces a variety of domestic small and medium-sized companies that have achieved continuous growth based on the smart factory project provided by Samsung Electronics as well as gives information on the technological competitiveness and the outlook for the companies in the global market. #SmartBizAccelerators #ArirangTV #smartfactory #smartfactoryproject #competitiveness_of_manufacturing #strengthening_competitiveness_of_SMEs #expanding_into_overseas_markets #growth_into_globalbusiness

programme.title: K-Sports Beyond
programme.desc: "Transcend the Limits of Sports — K-SPORTS BEYOND!“ Where the thrilling contest of sweat and passion meets the unrivaled innovation of Korea's sports industry. Beyond intuition, to precise data—transcending all limits! From real-time AI motion analysis and high-performance sportswear to protective gear, smart facilities, and next-gen fitness solutions, we set the new standard for the future of sports. Meet 20 promising Korean sports enterprises expanding onto the global stage! Our passionate hosts and international guests dive into everyday life and the field of play to verify, experience, and showcase the superior technology and craftsmanship of K-Sports in a 100% real variety show. Beyond innovation to a quantum leap! Running alongside the world, [K-Sports Beyond] begins now.

programme.title: Exploring Korean Literature
programme.desc: 2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They’ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel "One Left", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film "Parasite," and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel "Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel "Diary of a Murderer" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, "Hysteria," as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, "The Disaster Tourist", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->

programme.title: The Making of Kpop
programme.desc: How Did Kpop Captivate the World?Long before BTS and BLACKPINK became household names, pioneering artists and producers were breaking boundaries and shaping a new sound. Their passion and creativity laid the foundation for the Kpop we know and love today. The Making of Kpop takes us back to the pioneers and the music that started it all — tracing how Kpop emerged, evolved, and grew into a global cultural phenomenon. Behind the dazzling performances and infectious music we love, what stories remain untold? Join us on a journey back to Kpop's roots and discover the story behind the music that captivated the world. The Making of Kpop. Where the story begins. * YouTube: Sat 9:00 PM (KST)* TV Premiere: Fri 9:00 AM (KST)

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: The AI industry has just had the fright of its life. After a shock US midterm election result handed Democrats control of both houses of Congress, the companies leading the AI revolution suddenly face an uncomfortable reality: investigations, subpoenas, public backlash and the prospect of sweeping new regulation. At the very centre of the storm is Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose company sits at the heart of the global AI boom. Recent revelations surrounding Huang have triggered a crisis of confidence, wiped hundreds of billions from Nvidia's market value, and raised difficult questions about corporate governance, national security and the concentration of power inside the AI industry. Meanwhile, Elon Musk's political gamble appears to have backfired spectacularly. After pouring hundreds of millions of dollars into the midterms, Silicon Valley's most influential figures are now confronting a Congress that may be far less willing to give them the benefit of the doubt.

programme.title: The Interface
programme.desc: The show that reaches through your screen, to tell you the tech stories that ready matter. Hosted by BBC technology journalist Thomas Germain and social media expert Professor Jessica Maddox, The Interface dives into the stories, trends, apps, gadgets, algorithms and internet obsessions shaping how we live, work, think and connect. From AI and influencers to memes, data leaks, cybersecurity and the weirdest corners of the web, The Interface explores what happens when technology collides with real life. Cutting through the hype, the hosts unpack the platforms, products and online phenomena that increasingly shape our choices, our culture and our sense of self - whether we like it or not! Sharp, insightful and often very funny, The Interface examines our relationship with technology in all its messy, brilliant, absurd and world-changing glory. Along the way, it tackles one of the biggest questions of our age: what kind of future are the likes of Elon Musk, Chat GPT and all the other Silicon Valley giants building, and does anyone really want to live there?
